changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 3 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/5793-spec-range-floors.md`

- names `pnpm-lock.yaml` → `pnpm-lock.yaml` — edited by this change

  > Nothing a consumer installs today changes: normal resolution already picks the newest 17.x, and `pnpm-lock.yaml` still resolves 17.2.0 on this edge after the bump. The change is to the declared floor only, which is why it is scored `patch` rather than `minor` — the same reasoning objectui#5753 used for the other direction on this dependency.

### `.changeset/6361-spec-floor-17-2-0.md`

- names `pnpm-lock.yaml` → `pnpm-lock.yaml` — edited by this change

  > Nothing a consumer installs today changes: normal resolution already picks the newest 17.x, and `pnpm-lock.yaml` still resolves `17.2.0` on both edges after the bump — only the recorded `specifier:` moves. No source and no behaviour changes, which is why this is scored `patch`, on the reasoning `111741454` used for the same remediation on `@object-ui/plugin-detail`.

### `.changeset/7122-objectstack-family-17-3-0.md`

- names `pnpm-lock.yaml` → `pnpm-lock.yaml` — edited by this change

  > `@objectstack/client`, `core`, `formula` and `lint` each pin `@objectstack/spec` EXACTLY, so resolving the spec alone to 17.3.0 left the console bundling TWO copies of it. Moving the family with it in `pnpm-lock.yaml` collapses the duplicate; every declared range already admitted 17.3.0, so no manifest moved.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `cb2f6fb5b` (merge-base with origin/main): 8 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1824 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2434 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36747937419)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `70371d0aa65e0378bd3af20ecb13bb227dd351fe`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #8220 (body and all ten comments), PR #11239 (body, nine-file list, net diff against the merge-base `6f864cf62a` with `main`), the check-runs on the head, and the spec rows read at the `@objectstack/spec@17.5.0` tag commit (objectstack `0f6dcac5e9`). Nothing built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Population: four registrations, not six — right.** Read off each `index.tsx` at the head, not grepped. `packages/plugin-map/src/index.tsx:91` registers `object-map` only (the bare `map` twin retired by objectui#10393, pinned in `index.bareMapKeyRetired-10393.test.tsx`); `packages/plugin-gantt/src/index.tsx:139` registers `object-gantt` only (bare `gantt` retired by objectui#8008, pinned in `__tests__/bare-gantt-node-key-retired-8008.test.ts`); `packages/plugin-timeline/src/index.tsx:369` registers `object-timeline` and `:381` registers `view:timeline`. The fifth timeline registration, the presentational `plugin-timeline:timeline` (`renderer.tsx:1956`, `skipFallback: true`, `items` input), reads no `schema.filter`, `schema.sort`, `objectName` or `dataSource`, so declaring there would be declared without enforced; its exclusion is right. The dispatch's "all six" (5809921043) was a count taken on an older `main`; the ruling's shape — every registration of these renderers — is applied to exactly the registrations that exist, and all four gain both keys.

2. **Declared = enforced on each of the four — right.** `ObjectMap.tsx:857` holds `useResolvedFilter(schema.filter, filterScope)` and lowers it at `:951-952` (object fetch) and `:1030-1031` (inline rows) as `$filter` beside `$orderby: convertSortToQueryParams(schema.sort)`; `ObjectGantt.tsx:918` and `:1063-1064`, the one `find` its reload issues for every provider; `ObjectTimeline.tsx:362` and `:440-441`, the object query only, which authored `items`, host `data` or bound rows suppress — and the timeline input description says exactly that. Each pin's render rows mount every tag through the real `SchemaRenderer` and read `$filter` equal to the authored rule array and `$orderby` as the field-to-direction map, with an unauthored control that sends neither.

3. **Input shapes against the 17.5.0 rows — right.** At `0f6dcac5e9`, `packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts` maps `'object-map'` (`:5454`), `'object-gantt'` (`:5455`) and `'object-timeline'` (`:5473`) in `ComponentPropsMap`; no bare `timeline`, `map` or `gantt` row. Each row declares `filter: z.array(ViewFilterRuleSchema, { error: ruleArrayFilterError(…) }).optional()` (`:4565`, `:4750`, `:5158`) and `sort: z.array(SortItemSchema).optional()` (`:4591`, `:4758`, `:5166`). `ViewFilterRuleSchema` (`ui/view.zod.ts:941`) is a strict `{ field, operator, value? }`; `SortItemSchema` (`shared/enums.zod.ts:27`) is `{ field, order: asc | desc }`. The four registrations declare both keys `type: 'array'`, the descriptions naming `[{ field, operator, value }, ...]` and `[{ field, order }]` — the array arm, not the record, as the spec seat asked (5614374239). Precedent-consistent: kanban `filter` (`plugin-kanban/src/index.tsx:667`), calendar `filter` and `sort` (`plugin-calendar/src/index.tsx:419-420`) and grid (`plugin-grid/src/index.tsx:240`, `:258`) are all `type: 'array'` with no member arm.

4. **The record form now draws `type-mismatch` on the html tier — right.** `packages/sdui-parser/src/validate.ts:342-343` answers the `array` arm with `Array.isArray(value)`, so a MongoDB-style object is refused where it was passed through as `unknown-prop` before; the spec refuses the same value at `filter` on all three rows. Pinned on both faces (row 3 of each file).

5. **The tuple form the spec refuses passes the html tier — pre-existing, not introduced here.** The same `Array.isArray` arm accepts `[['status', '=', 'open']]` on these four doors exactly as it does on the kanban, calendar and grid `filter` inputs today; no precedent declaration is tighter. The vocabulary does hold a tightening the diff does not take: `of: 'object'` (objectui#8067's member arm, `validate.ts:396-425`, drawing `member-type-mismatch` on a tuple member), already used on `plugin-detail/src/index.tsx:631`'s `filter`. Its omission is consistent with the three precedents and with the dispatch shape (array arm versus record). Escalated in ③ as a follow-up, not a blocker.

6. **The `plugin-timeline` devDependency and the lockfile line — right.** `packages/plugin-timeline/package.json` gains one line, `"@object-ui/sdui-parser": "workspace:*"` under `devDependencies`, the field `plugin-map` (`:48`) and `plugin-gantt` (`:52`) already carry for the same import; the `pnpm-lock.yaml` diff is the three-line `link:../sdui-parser` importer entry under that package and nothing else — no resolution moved. Lockfile Integrity Check and Lockfile Dedupe Check concluded success on the head. Not a published surface; no changeset claim for it, and none is owed.

7. **The gate the dispatch cited does not exist; the substitutes judged nothing; the pins do — right, with one qualification.** `check:react-blocks-declaration-parity` is not a script in objectui's root `package.json` at the head (the only parity script there is `check:component-surface-parity`). In objectstack, `packages/spec/scripts/` holds only `build-react-blocks-contract.ts`, whose `check:react-blocks` generates the skills reference and reads no objectui registration; the cited name survives only in ADR-0082 and CHANGELOG prose — a content grep does hit those, so the dev's "zero hits" is true of scripts, not of text. The dev's two substitutes are not parity evidence for these blocks: `apps/console/src/__tests__/registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts` books all three in `UNJUDGED_SPEC_BLOCKS` (`:862-872`, owed to objectui#11168), and `scripts/check-component-surface-parity.mjs` looks the spec up by `site.fullType` (`:682`, `:1322`), which never matches a bare-keyed row — the dev's own acceptance note, verified. The parity evidence that does exist is row 6 of each pin (the installed row's `safeParse` accepts the authored values and refuses `bogusProp`) beside row 5 (the registration declares), per key on both faces, and this review's own read of the rows at the tag. Adequate for the two keys this card names.

8. **A same-class key outside this card's pair — observed, not judged here.** The `object-timeline` row also declares `limit` (`component.zod.ts:5168`), `ObjectTimeline.tsx:442` lowers `schema.limit` to `$top`, and neither timeline registration declares `limit`. The map and gantt renderers read no `limit` and their rows carry none. Escalated in ③.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/8220-map-gantt-timeline-query-inputs.md` declares `@object-ui/plugin-map`, `@object-ui/plugin-gantt` and `@object-ui/plugin-timeline` at `minor` — right. Two new declared inputs on each of four published registrations widen the manifest-driven authoring surface; nothing is removed; the level is the one `7712-kanban-calendar-filter-input.md` (calendar and kanban, minor) and `8171-calendar-sort-input.md` (calendar, minor) took for the same defect. The `sdui-parser` devDependency changes no published surface and is rightly not scored.

The body, read line by line: the four registrations named — right; the renderers lower `$filter` with context tokens resolved first and `$orderby` via `convertSortToQueryParams` — right; `validateTree` reports `unknown-prop` for every key no `inputs` entry claims (`validate.ts:227`) — right; the three blocks had no spec row when filed (the card at 17.2.0, the hold probe 5824695724 at 17.4.0) — right; 17.5.0 maps them with the two arrays — right at the tag; the record form is refused at all three doors and now draws `type-mismatch` on the html tier — right; `sort` takes `[{ field, order }]` — right; `view:timeline` declares the same pair as `object-timeline`, the `view:calendar` precedent — right; the bare twins retired by objectui#10393 and objectui#8008 — right; the pins as described (live-registry manifest, undeclared-key control, installed spec-row verdict, `SchemaRenderer` mount per tag) — right, every file carries those rows; the console ledger untouched and booking the blocks unjudged owed to objectui#11168 — right (`:862-872`). Changeset Declaration, Changeset Bump Policy, Changeset Fixed Group Check, Changeset Overwrite Report and Changeset Claim Re-read all concluded success on the head; the re-read names three pending changesets that mention `pnpm-lock.yaml`, each about `@objectstack/*` resolution, which this diff's one importer link does not move — their paragraphs stay true.

`Clause-②: yes` is declared on the claim (5913887919) and in the PR body: it sits on the body's line 3, after `Fixes #8220` on line 1 and a blank line 2 — not on the second line, which is empty. Consistent with the widening. The tier notice 5612086643 lifted the contract-review-tier requirement for this card, so this record is the lane seat's review of record.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev deviations, each answered:

1. File-surface extension (`packages/plugin-timeline/package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`) — accepted: the one remedy `check:phantom-deps` prescribes, identical to the sibling plugins' line, declared in the body (①6).
2. Four registrations, not six — verified at the head; accepted (①1).
3. Named gate absent — verified in both repos; the substitutes judge nothing for these blocks, the pins do; accepted (①7).
4. The pin-file red and green runs outside the verify lock — the head's check-runs are the gate verdicts; nothing is adopted from the report's local runs.
5. Lint narrowed to three packages — Lint concluded success on the head; moot.
6. One pin file per plugin carrying declaration and render rows — accepted; every tag has a render row and an unauthored control.
7. `main` merged mid-run — the head is that merge; the net diff against the merge-base `6f864cf62a` is the nine files and nothing else; accepted.
8. Commit trailers spelled per the repo's own convention — a repo-convention matter, not a contract item; noted.

`open_questions`: empty — nothing to answer.

`out_of_scope_findings`, each answered:

- Html tier cannot tell the rule array from the tuple form — pre-existing across every `filter` input, not introduced here (①5). Follow-up for the seat: `of: 'object'` on the `filter` doors (these four, plus kanban, calendar and grid) is the tightening the vocabulary already holds; alternatively objectui#11168's `MEMBER_PINS` once it loads these plugins. Neither blocks this card.
- `check:component-surface-parity` never matches a spec row for a plugin-namespaced registration — verified at `:682` and `:1322`; a real defect in a report-only tool, unfiled; the seat may file it.
- `packages/plugin-timeline/README.md` documents only the presentational tag — pre-existing; noted.
